why: Two panes of ONE puzzle3d document: each world surface must name the window it was mounted into, and must publish the selection it actually paints. Before wave B20 both panes reported data-surface-id="1" (the per-document DFS record id, minted identically in every window) and published no selection at all — WorldInteractionRecord carries no selectedIds/hoverTarget, data-instances-json is the guest's geometry cache which never bakes selection, and data-status-json is the off-thread compute status.

selectionPublication.why: selection is per DOCUMENT (both panes carry the same selectedIds), hover is per WINDOW (each pane publishes its own hoverTarget), and the armed utility is per window instance (wave B9). The overlay that supplies the ids supplies the ACTIVE one too: the gumball target, Inspection's focus and `data-selection-json` all read the single `activeObjectId` field instead of the list, so an overlay that replaced the list and left it null published `{selectedIds:[picked], activeObjectId:null}` for the whole window it was covering — measured on the 180-object Nakagin document, every sample of a 12-minute run (wave B46).

guestPublished.why: data-guest-selection-json is the guest's OWN unmerged lane. On this exact fixture the pane PAINTS seed-left-001 while the guest sent nothing, and before wave B23 no attribute anywhere separated those two readings — which is why six waves could not tell 'the guest lost the pick' from 'the host is painting it for the guest'.

guestCarriedPick.why: The other side of the discriminator: when the guest DID keep the pick, its own lane says so — so `data-guest-selection-json` separates the two readings in both directions, not only when the guest is empty.
